910.name: Caucasian Albania and Ancient Azerbaijani Lands
910.description: The early civilizations of the eastern Transcaucasus, Mannaea, and the emergence of Caucasian Albania as a distinct political and cultural entity in the territories of modern Azerbaijan.

sub_clusters.name: Mannaea and Early Cultures
sub_clusters.description: The kingdom of Mannaea in the Lake Urmia region, Scythian and Cimmerian incursions, and the pre-Iranian cultures of the Azerbaijani highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Achaemenid Period and Atropatene
sub_clusters.description: The region under Achaemenid Persian rule, the emergence of Media Atropatene (the etymological root of 'Azerbaijan') following Alexander's conquests, and the Zoroastrian fire temples.
key_events: Atropates establishes Media Atropatene as an independent kingdom (c. 323 BC)
Zoroastrian fire temples flourish at sites like Ateshgah

910.name: Caucasian Albania — Classical Period
910.description: The Kingdom of Caucasian Albania as a major Transcaucasian state, its unique alphabet and Church, Roman and Parthian influences, and its Christianization.

sub_clusters.name: Caucasian Albanian Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Caucasian Albania as a federation of 26 tribes between the Greater Caucasus and the Kura-Araxes rivers, its interactions with Rome and Parthia, and its distinct culture.

sub_clusters.name: Christianization of Caucasian Albania
sub_clusters.description: The adoption of Christianity, the creation of the Caucasian Albanian alphabet by Mesrop Mashtots, and growing Sassanid Persian pressure on the region.

920.name: Arab Conquest and Islamic Azerbaijani States
920.description: The Arab Muslim conquest and Islamization of Azerbaijan, the rise of local Islamic dynasties including the Shirvanshahs, Sajids, Sallarids, and Rawadids.

sub_clusters.name: Arab Conquest and Islamization
sub_clusters.description: The Rashidun and Umayyad conquests of Azerbaijan, the displacement of Zoroastrianism and Christianity by Islam, and the incorporation into the Caliphate.
key_events: Arab forces conquer Azerbaijan and Caucasian Albania (642–667 AD)
Mass conversion to Islam transforms the region's religious landscape

sub_clusters.name: Shirvanshah Dynasty — Rise
sub_clusters.description: The establishment and growth of the Shirvanshah dynasty ruling from Shamakhi, the longest-reigning dynasty in the Islamic world, and its role as a cultural center.

sub_clusters.name: Local Islamic Dynasties
sub_clusters.description: The Sajid, Sallarid, Shaddadid, and Rawadid dynasties that governed parts of Azerbaijan, their cultural patronage and rivalry, and the Seljuk Turkic influx.

920.name: Seljuk and Atabeg Period
920.description: The Seljuk Turkic conquest and the Turkification of Azerbaijan, the flourishing Atabeg state of Azerbaijan (Eldiguzids), and the zenith of medieval Azerbaijani culture.

sub_clusters.name: Seljuk Turkification
sub_clusters.description: The Great Seljuk conquest that brought waves of Oghuz Turkic migration, fundamentally transforming the linguistic and ethnic character of Azerbaijan.

sub_clusters.name: Eldiguzid Atabeg State
sub_clusters.description: The powerful Atabeg state of Azerbaijan under the Eldiguzid dynasty, the poet Nizami Ganjavi's literary masterpieces, and the golden age of Azerbaijani culture.
key_events: Nizami Ganjavi composes the Khamsa, a masterwork of Persian literature (1177–1209)
Eldiguzid capital Tabriz becomes a major commercial and cultural center

930.name: Mongol and Timurid Azerbaijan
930.description: The Mongol invasions, Azerbaijan as the heartland of the Ilkhanate with Tabriz as its capital, and the subsequent Timurid and Turkmen periods.

sub_clusters.name: Ilkhanate and Tabriz as Capital
sub_clusters.description: Azerbaijan as the political center of the Mongol Ilkhanate, Tabriz and Sultaniyya as imperial capitals, Rashid al-Din's historiographic works, and cultural synthesis.
key_events: Hulagu Khan establishes the Ilkhanate with Tabriz as capital (1256)
Rashid al-Din compiles the Jami al-Tawarikh, a universal history (c. 1307)

sub_clusters.name: Turkmen Tribal Confederations
sub_clusters.description: The Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen states centered in Azerbaijan, their rivalries, and their role in shaping Azerbaijani Turkic identity.

930.name: Safavid Origins and Azerbaijani Heartland
930.description: The rise of the Safavid order in Ardabil, the establishment of the Safavid Empire with Azerbaijani Turkic Qizilbash warriors, and the imposition of Twelver Shia Islam.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of the Safavids from Ardabil
sub_clusters.description: Shah Ismail I's unification of Iran from Tabriz using Azerbaijani Qizilbash warriors, the establishment of Shia Islam as state religion, and the foundational role of Azerbaijani Turkic culture in the empire.
key_events: Shah Ismail I conquers Tabriz and founds the Safavid Empire (1501)
Battle of Chaldiran against the Ottomans shapes the Safavid-Ottoman frontier (1514)

sub_clusters.name: Safavid Azerbaijani Provinces
sub_clusters.description: Azerbaijan's role within the Safavid state, the shifting of the capital from Tabriz to Isfahan, Ottoman-Safavid wars over Azerbaijani territory, and the Shirvanshah legacy.

940.name: Khanates and Russian Conquest
940.description: The fragmentation of Azerbaijan into semi-independent khanates after the Safavid collapse, and the Russian imperial conquest of the Caucasus absorbing Azerbaijani territories.

sub_clusters.name: Azerbaijani Khanates
sub_clusters.description: The independent khanates of Baku, Shirvan, Sheki, Karabakh, Nakhchivan, and others — their governance, conflicts, and cultural life in the post-Safavid power vacuum.

sub_clusters.name: Russian Annexation
sub_clusters.description: The Russo-Persian wars ending with the treaties of Gulistan (1813) and Turkmenchay (1828), dividing Azerbaijan between Russian and Qajar Persian control.
key_events: Treaty of Gulistan cedes northern Azerbaijani khanates to Russia (1813)
Treaty of Turkmenchay completes the partition of Azerbaijan (1828)

sub_clusters.name: Baku Oil Boom
sub_clusters.description: The discovery and exploitation of Baku's massive oil reserves, the Nobel Brothers and Rothschild investments, the transformation of Baku into a world oil capital, and the rise of an Azerbaijani bourgeoisie.
key_events: First modern oil well drilled at Bibi-Heybat near Baku (1846)
Baku produces over half the world's oil supply (1901)

950.name: Democratic Republic and Sovietization
950.description: The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic — the first secular democratic republic in the Muslim world — and its swift conquest by the Red Army.

sub_clusters.name: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic
sub_clusters.description: The establishment of the ADR on May 28, 1918, its progressive constitution granting women's suffrage, the March Days violence, and the Bolshevik invasion ending independence.
key_events: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic proclaimed — first secular democratic republic in the Muslim world (1918)
Red Army invades and sovietizes Azerbaijan (April 1920)

sub_clusters.name: March Days and Ethnic Conflict
sub_clusters.description: The March Days massacre in Baku, Armenian-Azerbaijani communal violence, and the Shusha events shaping lasting intercommunal tensions.

950.name: Soviet Azerbaijan
950.description: Azerbaijan as a Soviet republic: the oil industry under central planning, Stalinist repression, Heydar Aliyev's rise, the Nagorno-Karabakh crisis, and Black January.

sub_clusters.name: Stalinist Era and Oil Industry
sub_clusters.description: Soviet industrialization centered on Baku oil, the crucial role of Baku oil in WWII, Stalinist purges of Azerbaijani intelligentsia, and the forced assimilation of national identity.

sub_clusters.name: Aliyev Era and National Consciousness
sub_clusters.description: Heydar Aliyev's leadership of Soviet Azerbaijan as Communist Party First Secretary, economic development, patronage networks, and the cultivation of national cadres.

sub_clusters.name: Black January and Independence Movement
sub_clusters.description: The Nagorno-Karabakh crisis, the Sumgait and Baku pogroms, Soviet military crackdown on Black January (1990), and the declaration of independence.
key_events: Black January — Soviet troops kill over 130 civilians in Baku (January 20, 1990)
Azerbaijan declares independence from the Soviet Union (October 1991)

960.name: Independent Azerbaijan and Karabakh Wars
960.description: Post-Soviet Azerbaijan's wars over Nagorno-Karabakh, the oil-fueled economic boom under the Aliyev dynasty, and the decisive 2020 military victory.

sub_clusters.name: First Karabakh War and Displacement
sub_clusters.description: The devastating First Nagorno-Karabakh War, Azerbaijani military defeats, the loss of Karabakh and seven surrounding districts, and over 600,000 internally displaced persons.

sub_clusters.name: Contract of the Century and Oil Boom
sub_clusters.description: Heydar Aliyev's 'Contract of the Century' with Western oil companies, the BTC pipeline, massive oil revenues, Baku's transformation, and the consolidation of Ilham Aliyev's authoritarian rule.
key_events: Contract of the Century signed with international oil consortium (1994)
Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline inaugurated (2006)

sub_clusters.name: Second Karabakh War and Victory
sub_clusters.description: The 44-day war in 2020 recapturing surrounding districts with Turkish support, the 2023 offensive reclaiming Nagorno-Karabakh entirely, and Azerbaijan's regional ascendancy.
key_events: 44-day war ends with Azerbaijani victory and trilateral ceasefire (November 2020)
Azerbaijan recaptures Nagorno-Karabakh; Armenian population flees (September 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
